claims.text: In as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys, magnetocaloric response and hysteresis under low-applied-field cooling cycles are governed by the interplay between phase distribution, phase morphology, and magnetic domain structure.
Changing substrate temperature, deposition rate, or annealing conditions can controllably alter the alloy microstructure.
The relevant structural mediator is the distribution and morphology of phases.
Phase distribution and morphology influence the magnetic domain structure.
The magnetic domain structure affects the magnetocaloric response.
The magnetic domain structure affects hysteresis.
An optimized microstructure will improve magnetocaloric response relative to the as-deposited baseline.
An optimized microstructure will reduce hysteresis relative to the as-deposited baseline.
An optimized microstructure will enhance heat-exchange rates relative to the as-deposited baseline.
The predictions apply to microstructures tunable by deposition-parameter manipulation while avoiding rare-earth elements and retaining mechanical stability and low cost.
Failure of the optimized microstructure to improve magnetocaloric response, reduce hysteresis, and enhance heat-exchange rates would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The target and baseline are described as as-deposited, but annealing is included as an intervention; annealed specimens are no longer strictly in the as-deposited state.
